title: Emit provider-run telemetry from the daemon activation path
description:
Objective: give `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` and `parseClaudeResultTelemetry` their FIRST production call sites in apps/, so the daemon actually observes a provider run instead of merely being able to.

MEASURED GAP at HEAD ac09ca9, symbol by symbol. `grep -rn "launchClaude" --include=*.ts apps` returns ZERO hits — nothing in apps/ launches a provider through the telemetry seam at all. The producers are landed and published: `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` (packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/claude-telemetry-launch.ts:206, published at surface/claude-surface.ts:185), `parseClaudeResultTelemetry` (claude-result-telemetry.ts:214, published at claude-surface.ts:175), and the `ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` shape (claude-telemetry-launch.ts:70). apps/daemon's ONLY `ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` mention is a COMMENT at telemetry/provider-run-contracts.ts:84, not a call site.

WHERE IT BELONGS, and why this is not the agent spawner. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/* spawns moe's own agent wrappers through `node:child_process` (agent-spawn-contract.ts:9) — a different concern. The provider-run seam is the ACTIVATION path: apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ingress.ts already imports `activateEffect` / `applyEffectCommand` / `EffectIntent` from @moe/runner. The ledger's own identity confirms it — `deriveProviderRunAggregateId` keys on provider, runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch, and effectIntentId/attemptRef are activation vocabulary.

Deliverable: a daemon activation-side telemetry launch module that takes an admitted effect intent plus its attempt slice, launches through `launchClaudeWithTelemetry`, parses the result through `parseClaudeResultTelemetry`, and returns the `ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` or an existing stable refusal. No new refusal vocabulary — reuse what the runner already publishes.

NOT in scope: building or committing a ProviderRunRecord (that is the sibling task, which consumes this handoff), budget authority, benchmark harness, corpus, or scoring.

Owned paths: apps/daemon/src/activation/ (one new module + its .js bridge + its .test.ts). Do NOT publish it from apps/daemon/src/index.ts.

Cross-package edge is pre-verified: apps/daemon/package.json declares "@moe/runner": "workspace:*" and pnpm-lock carries the importer, with durable bare-specifier call sites already at activation-ingress.ts:1. Still run the compiled probe per the workspace-dep rail.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test — read the OUTPUT count line, not the exit code. Daemon gates are red at baseline from foreign in-flight slices; apply the path-attributed baseline over the owned paths.
definitionOfDone: `grep -rn "launchClaudeWithTelemetry\|parseClaudeResultTelemetry" --include=*.ts apps | grep -v '\.test\.'` returns AT LEAST ONE production call site in apps/daemon — the count was zero before this task and the assertion is on the production surface, not a test.

A refusal from the launch or the parse is returned with the runner's own stable reason code and refusing layer preserved verbatim, never re-wrapped into a new daemon code; a test asserts the exact code AND which layer answered.

A successful launch returns a `ClaudeTelemetryHandoff` built by the runner, never a daemon-composed lookalike; a mutation that swaps the real handoff for a locally-shaped object turns a NAMED test red.

No caller-supplied timing pair, model snapshot, or reasoning effort can reach the handoff — those are production observations; a test drives a hostile input asserting the caller-supplied value is not echoed.
The new module carries a physical one-line .js bridge, each production source is under 250 physical lines by `grep -c ''`, and apps/daemon/src/index.ts is unmodified.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` run with their exit codes captured separately; the test leg prints a nonzero Test Files/Tests count line, and the HEAD-minus-merge-base failing-path delta intersected with the owned paths is EMPTY.
taskRails: Use the runner's published surfaces through the BARE specifier `@moe/runner`; do not deep-import into packages/runner/src/** and do not reimplement launch, parse, or refusal authority inside apps/daemon.
Fail closed with the runner's existing stable reason codes. A launch or parse that cannot be observed stays UNKNOWN and never gains authority.
This is a production emission task, not a proof task: no mock provider may stand in for the real seam in the production path. Test doubles are permitted only inside tests.
Preserve foreign work; commit only the explicit owned paths by pathspec — never a bare `git commit`, never `git add -A`. The index is shared state in this single working directory.

implementationPlan.description:
BASELINE, AND LEARN THE ONE THING THAT WILL OTHERWISE BE GOT WRONG. Re-measure the producer on current bytes (measured at HEAD abc3dcf) before naming a symbol.
**`ok: true` DOES NOT MEAN THE RUN SUCCEEDED.** `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` (claude-telemetry-launch.ts:206) returns `ClaudeTelemetryLaunchResult` = `{ok:true, handoff}` | `ProviderTelemetryRefusal`, and the ONLY path to the refusal arm is a malformed run ref (`telemetryRefusal("TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED", "TELEMETRY_INPUT")`, :214). A launcher that REFUSED before any bytes existed, and a delivery that launched no process at all, BOTH return `ok:true` carrying a BLIND handoff whose facts are UNKNOWN and whose `telemetryRefusal` field is populated (:217-224). So a consumer that branches on `ok` alone reports a refused launch as a healthy observation. Read `handoff.terminal`, `handoff.infrastructure` and `handoff.telemetryRefusal`, never `ok` alone.
**PARSE IS ALREADY COMPOSED.** :227 calls `parseClaudeResultTelemetry({providerRunRef, stdout: observation.stdout})` INSIDE the launch. Do NOT call it again from the daemon — that would double-parse the same bytes. This task's DoD grep is an OR and is satisfied by the launch call site alone; the description's prose implying two calls is looser than the measured surface, and the surface wins.
**THE RUN REF IS PLAIN DATA IN, VALIDATED INSIDE.** `ClaudeTelemetryLaunchInput.providerRunRef` is typed `unknown` (:65) and the launch snapshots it. `snapshotRunRef` is deliberately withheld from the package root (claude-surface.ts:160 states this). So pass a plain `{provider:"claude", runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch}` object — the five fields at provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:141-147 — and let the runner validate. Never mint, normalize or bound-check a run ref in apps/daemon; that is reimplementing a withheld minter.
Also confirm the gap this task closes is still open: `grep -rn "launchClaude" --include=*.ts apps` returns ZERO. If it now returns hits, stop and re-measure — someone else may have landed the edge.
GATES, each run separately with its own exit code — never `;`-chained (only the last status survives), never piped into tail (tail's status is reported): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, recording the count line and EVERY failing file as your before-set. Both are expected RED from foreign in-flight slices; repair none of it.

DoD 4 is stronger on the blind arm, where launch.startedAt/completedAt are null and observedModel is UNKNOWN, so any echo of a caller value is visible. I will pin (a)(b)(c)+hostile input and disclose the OBSERVED measurement rather than fake an observed run.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED — write the cases that distinguish the three outcomes `ok` cannot. Create `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.test.ts` importing the not-yet-existing module and watch it fail to resolve. Then pin, each asserting the exact stable code AND the answering layer from `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS` (TELEMETRY_INPUT, TELEMETRY_LAUNCH, TELEMETRY_CAPTURE, TELEMETRY_SCHEMA, TELEMETRY_RESULT — five layers can answer, so a code-only assertion detaches the moment a different one answers first):
(a) MALFORMED RUN REF — the only true refusal arm: assert `ok:false`, code `TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED`, layer `TELEMETRY_INPUT`. Drive it with a genuinely malformed ref (the bounded-ref alphabet is `/^[!-~]{1,200}$/u`), not a plausible-looking one.
(b) LAUNCH REFUSED — assert `ok:true` AND that the module does NOT report it as an observation: `handoff.telemetryRefusal` is populated with `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED`, and the handoff's facts are UNKNOWN rather than zero. This is the case that catches a consumer branching on `ok` alone.
(c) LAUNCH NOT ATTEMPTED — same shape, `TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED`; assert it is distinguishable from (b), since both are `ok:true` blind handoffs and collapsing them loses which happened.
(d) OBSERVED — a real launch returns a handoff whose `providerRunRef` equals the five identity facts passed in, whose `handoffVersion` and `parserVersion` are the runner's constants, and whose token/step observations are the runner's, not defaults invented locally.
Assert once across the file that NO case yields a truth class above UNKNOWN except a genuinely observed run, and that no case renders an UNKNOWN fact as zero — an unmeasured token count and a zero token count are different facts.
implementationPlan.note:

Focused command that actually narrows (the pnpm script's own `src` arg unions with an appended path instead of intersecting it, so `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test <path>` runs all 99 files): from apps/daemon, `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.test.ts`.

SIX CASES PINNED, each on the exact code AND the answering layer:
(a) malformed run ref — ok:false, TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED / TELEMETRY_INPUT. Driven by a runRef containing a SPACE, genuinely outside the bounded alphabet /^[!-~]{1,200}$/u.
(b) LAUNCH REFUSED — ok:TRUE, telemetryRefusal TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED / TELEMETRY_LAUNCH, terminal REFUSED, infrastructure LAUNCH_REFUSED, and the launcher's own reasonCode/reasonLayer forwarded unwrapped. The refusal is a real production one from the pre-open selection gate (argv names sonnet, selection names opus), not a request too malformed to survive the snapshot.
(c) LAUNCH NOT ATTEMPTED — TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED / TELEMETRY_LAUNCH, terminal UNKNOWN, infrastructure LAUNCH_NOT_ATTEMPTED, launch.kind EXIT_BEFORE_LAUNCH. Reached through the REAL `resolveDuplicateDelivery` port with no injected deps at all, because duplicate resolution sits ahead of every other phase. Four fields are asserted DIFFERENT from (b) so the two ok:true blind arms cannot collapse into one.
(d) replaced, with the measurement in the file header rather than a quiet narrowing — OBSERVED is unreachable from apps/daemon (four of the ten launcher ports have no published implementation; TS2305 on each). In its place, a NAMED case pins that the handoff is the RUNNER's: handoffVersion and parserVersion are the published constants, providerRunRef is a fresh frozen five-key snapshot (toEqual the input, NOT toBe it, and the key set pinned exactly), and handoff/tokens/launch are all deep-frozen — a daemon-composed lookalike built from spreads satisfies the field names and fails these.
(e) unmeasured-never-zero — sweeps both blind arms, asserts the sweep produced 2 cases, and requires every token/step/sequence/receipt/model fact to be `{known:false, code, layer}` with `not.toHaveProperty("value")`.
(f) hostile input for DoD 4 — plants startedAt, completedAt, observedModel, tokens, terminal and infrastructure on the caller's request under the exact names the handoff carries, then asserts launch.startedAt/completedAt are null, observedModel and tokens are UNKNOWN, terminal is UNKNOWN, and the observed model stringifies without the caller's model id or reasoning effort. The declared effort stays where the caller DOES have standing, on `declared`.

ONE SUBTLETY PINNED DELIBERATELY: on the NOT_ATTEMPTED arm `launch.truthClass` is "PROVEN" — it is proven that no process started, which is not a proven RUN. The test pins it with that reasoning beside it, because a consumer reading that flag as run authority is the same misread as branching on `ok`.

FOREIGN RED MOVED under me during this step: the full-suite run now shows agent-wrapper.test.ts at 15 failures / 4 errors versus 5 failures at my baseline minutes earlier. Same single foreign file, actively being edited by its owner. I will settle the step-6 delta on the failing FILE SET, not on counts.

implementationPlan.description:
IMPLEMENT THE EMISSION SEAM. Create `apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-telemetry-launch.ts` plus its one-line `.js` bridge (`export * from "./activation-telemetry-launch.ts";`, LF ending — apps/daemon requires a physical bridge per production module and the guard byte-compares, so CRLF or a trailing blank line lands it in `wrongContent`).
Public surface: bounded plain input only — the five run-identity facts, the launch request, and optional launch options. Return the runner's `ClaudeTelemetryLaunchResult` UNCHANGED, or a shape that preserves both arms losslessly. Do NOT re-wrap the refusal into a daemon code, do NOT flatten the blind-handoff arm into a boolean, and do NOT add a daemon-local success/failure verdict — the handoff already carries `terminal`, `infrastructure` and `telemetryRefusal`, and a second verdict layer would become a competing authority.
ONE call to `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` through the BARE specifier `@moe/runner`. No separate `parseClaudeResultTelemetry` call. No deep import into `packages/runner/src/**`.
ERROR MESSAGES: `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_MESSAGES` are deliberately static and non-interpolating because a message quoting captured bytes, the model or a digest would echo provider output back out of a failure path (provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:92-95). Do not add interpolation, do not append a path, argv, environment value or digest to any message this module produces.
Keep the production source under 250 physical lines — measure with `grep -c ''`, since PowerShell `Measure-Object -Line` undercounts. Do NOT publish from `apps/daemon/src/index.ts`; index-surface.test.ts pins an exact export count and index.ts is not an owned path here.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. Focused suite "Test Files 1 passed (1)", "Tests 7 passed (7)", EXIT=0. `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck` EXIT=0 with zero errors naming either of my files.

MODULE. `launchActivationProviderRun({providerRun, request, options?}) => Promise<ClaudeTelemetryLaunchResult>`. ONE call to `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` through the bare `@moe/runner`; no `parseClaudeResultTelemetry` call (the launch composes it); no deep import; no daemon verdict, no re-wrapped code, no flattened arm; the runner's result is returned as it arrived. Nothing interpolates a path, argv, environment value or digest, and the module produces no string on any failure path — the runner's static message travels with its own code and layer.

ONE DESIGN DECISION WORTH THE REVIEW. `providerRun` is forwarded VERBATIM rather than projected field by field. Rebuilding it would run the caller's accessors ahead of `snapshotRunRef`'s proxy guard, which refuses a proxy BEFORE reading any property — the caller's code executing inside the read that decides whether to trust the caller. The typed `ActivationProviderRunIdentity` names the five facts at compile time and is explicitly not a runtime check; the runner remains the only minter.

`options` is conditionally spread rather than passed as possibly-undefined: tsconfig.base.json sets exactOptionalPropertyTypes.

TWO REAL FINDINGS FROM THE RED, both of which changed the tests rather than the module.

1. My first hostile fixture was ANSWERED BY THE WRONG GUARD. Planting startedAt/completedAt/observedModel/tokens at the request's top level made `snapshotClaudeLaunchRequest` refuse the whole request — it reads an EXACT record — so the case came back TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED where it asserted NOT_ATTEMPTED. It was proving "a malformed request is refused", not "an observation is never echoed". Rewritten to plant the same values in `effect`, `attempt` and `runtime.quotedObservation` — fields the caller legitimately supplies as plain data — so the request is valid at the snapshot AND at the duplicate resolver and only the observation discipline can answer. It now also scans the WHOLE serialized handoff for the planted sentinel and for the planted timestamp, so it catches an echo into a field the case never thought to name.

2. That discovery earned its own NAMED case rather than being discarded: "refuses a request that carries handoff-shaped observation fields at the top level" pins CLAUDE_LAUNCH_REQUEST_MALFORMED / LAUNCHER wrapped as TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED / TELEMETRY_LAUNCH. It closes the smuggling route from the other side — the fields do not travel and are not silently dropped either.

SIZES by `grep -c ''`: production 97 lines (cap 250), bridge 1, test 333. Bridge bytes verified with `od -c`: `export * from "./activation-telemetry-launch.ts";\n` — single line, LF, no trailing blank, byte-pattern identical to the activation-embargo.js sibling. apps/daemon/src/index.ts unmodified (`git status --porcelain` on it is empty).

implementationPlan.description:

Cases (b) and (c) from step 2 MUST redden — they are the only tests that can, because both are `ok:true`. If they stay green, those assertions never distinguished a blind handoff from an observed one and must be strengthened before this task completes; report that finding either way. (2) Replace the returned handoff with a locally-shaped lookalike carrying the same field names; a NAMED test must redden, proving the handoff is the runner's and not a daemon composition. (3) Make the module normalize or bound-check the run ref before passing it, and confirm the malformed-ref case still refuses at `TELEMETRY_INPUT` — if it now refuses at a daemon layer instead, the module has grown a competing validator and the drill has found it. (4) Render one UNKNOWN token fact as zero and confirm a NAMED test reddens — an unmeasured count and a zero count are different facts.
For EVERY drill record the exact replaced range you edited: a drill that applied nothing reads as green and proves nothing. Confirm each red lands on the INTENDED assertion, not an unrelated crash or compile error. Restore with `git checkout -- <the one drilled file>` (never by hand — a hand restore goes ambiguous) and verify `git status --short` shows it clean before the next; a foreign whole-tree completion hook can otherwise commit a drill you left on disk.
implementationPlan.note:
FOUR DRILLS, each run alone, each red on its INTENDED assertion, each restored and hash-verified.

That is impossible here and would have been destructive: all three of my files are UNTRACKED (`git ls-files --error-unmatch` -> "did not match any file(s) known to git"), so there is no HEAD blob to check out. All four restores matched that sha exactly. Every drill was applied by an anchored single-occurrence replacement that asserted `count == 1` and PRINTED the replaced range, so no drill could apply nothing and read as green.

DRILL 1 — the headline. Replaced the return with `if (result.ok) return {ok:true, handoff:{...result.handoff, telemetryRefusal:null, terminal:"COMPLETED", infrastructure:"NONE"}}` — branch on `ok` alone, report every ok:true as healthy. Post-drill sha 66e7c418. RED: 5 failed / 2 passed, and BOTH plan-named cases are in it — "reports a REFUSED launch as a blind handoff, never as an observation" and "reports a delivery that launched nothing as NOT_ATTEMPTED, distinct from REFUSED". Landing assertion quoted: `expected null to deeply equal {ok:false, code:"TELEMETRY_LAUNCH_REFUSED", layer:"TELEMETRY_LAUNCH", message:"the launcher refused before any provider bytes existed"}` — the drill's null where the runner's refusal belongs. ANSWER TO THE STEP'S QUESTION: the assertions were NOT vacuous. They genuinely distinguish a blind handoff from an observed one, so no strengthening was required.

DRILL 2 — lookalike handoff. Rebuilt the handoff locally with ALL FIFTEEN field names and the runner's own values copied across, changing only that it was daemon-composed. RED, and precisely one test: "returns the runner's own handoff, not a daemon-composed lookalike". Landing assertion: `expected false to be true` on `Object.isFrozen(handoff)` — the producer deep-freezes, a spread-built lookalike does not. A lookalike that satisfies every field name still cannot pass.

DRILL 3 — competing validator. Added a daemon-side normalizer ahead of the call: trim, collapse whitespace to "-", slice to 200, coerce epoch through Math.trunc. RED, precisely one test: "refuses a malformed run ref at TELEMETRY_INPUT and launches nothing", `expected true to be false` on `result.ok` — the normalizer turned "run ref with a space" into the valid "run-ref-with-a-space", so the runner no longer refused. This is the sharper form of the plan's drill: rather than moving WHICH layer refuses, it removes the refusal entirely, and the test catches that the module must not touch the ref.

DRILL 4 — UNKNOWN rendered as zero. Replaced `tokens.inputTokens` with `{known:true, value:0}`. RED on the NAMED test "renders every unmeasured fact as UNKNOWN carrying its code, never as zero" (plus two others). planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD abc3dcf. I filed this task myself from a Clause-2 gap audit on task-b937811e; planning it required measuring the producer's SHAPE, which the audit did not need. Two findings materially refine the description I wrote.

FINDING 1 — `ok: true` DOES NOT MEAN SUCCESS, and this is the task's central hazard. `launchClaudeWithTelemetry` (claude-telemetry-launch.ts:206) returns `{ok:true, handoff}` | `ProviderTelemetryRefusal`, and the ONLY route to the refusal arm is a malformed run ref (`telemetryRefusal("TELEMETRY_RUN_REF_MALFORMED", "TELEMETRY_INPUT")` at :214). A launcher that REFUSED before any bytes existed (:217-219) and a delivery that launched nothing (:220-223) BOTH return `ok:true` with a BLIND handoff — facts UNKNOWN, `telemetryRefusal` populated inside the handoff. A consumer branching on `ok` alone reports a refused launch as a healthy observation, and every test would still pass. The real verdict lives in `handoff.terminal`, `handoff.infrastructure`, `handoff.telemetryRefusal`.

FINDING 2 — PARSE IS ALREADY COMPOSED. :227 calls `parseClaudeResultTelemetry({providerRunRef, stdout: observation.stdout})` inside the launch. The daemon needs ONE call, not two; calling parse again would double-parse the same bytes. The DoD grep I wrote is an OR, so it is satisfied by the launch site alone — the description's prose implying two calls is looser than the measured surface, and the surface wins.

INPUT CONTRACT. `ClaudeTelemetryLaunchInput` (:65) is `{providerRunRef: unknown; request: unknown; options?: ClaudeLaunchOptions}`. `providerRunRef` is `unknown` BY DESIGN: the launch snapshots and validates it, and `snapshotRunRef` is deliberately withheld from the package root (claude-surface.ts:160 says so explicitly, alongside `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_MESSAGES`). So the daemon passes plain data — the five fields at provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:141-147, `{provider:"claude", runRef, effectIntentId, attemptRef, epoch}`, bounded by `/^[!-~]{1,200}$/u` — and never mints or bound-checks one locally.

HANDOFF SHAPE (:70-86): handoffVersion, parserVersion, providerRunRef, launch, declared, observedModel, terminal, infrastructure, tokens, steps, sequence, concurrency, stdoutReceiptDigest, stderrReceiptDigest, telemetryRefusal.

FIVE LAYERS CAN REFUSE: `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_LAYERS` = TELEMETRY_INPUT, TELEMETRY_LAUNCH, TELEMETRY_CAPTURE, TELEMETRY_SCHEMA, TELEMETRY_RESULT. The contract's own comment (provider-telemetry-contracts.ts:80-85) warns that a test pinning only the code stays green once a different layer starts answering first.

MESSAGE HYGIENE IS A DECLARED RULE, not a style note: `PROVIDER_TELEMETRY_MESSAGES` are static and non-interpolating because "a message quoting the captured bytes, the model or a digest would echo provider output back out of a failure path" (:92-95). The daemon must not add interpolation.

WHERE IT LIVES. The activation path is the right home — `activation-ingress.ts` (321 lines; `runEffectActivateCommand` at :286, `ActivationStageResult` at :154) already imports `activateEffect`/`applyEffectCommand`/`EffectIntent` from the bare `@moe/runner` at :1, which is also the durable proof the cross-package edge is live. The ledger's identity keys on effectIntentId/attemptRef, both activation vocabulary. The orchestrator is NOT the home: it spawns moe's own agent wrappers via node:child_process.

planningNotes.risks:
1) `ok: true` IS NOT SUCCESS. The single most likely defect, and it ships green: only a malformed run ref reaches the refusal arm, so a consumer branching on `ok` reports refused and never-attempted launches as healthy observations. Step 2 cases (b) and (c) and drill 1 exist solely for this; if drill 1 leaves them green, those assertions never distinguished a blind handoff from an observed one.

2) DOUBLE PARSE. `parseClaudeResultTelemetry` is already called inside the launch. A second call is easy to add because this task's own description names both symbols.

3) A DAEMON-SIDE RUN-REF VALIDATOR. Tempting because `unknown` looks unsafe. It is a second copy of a deliberately withheld minter, and it moves which layer refuses — drill 3 detects exactly that by requiring the malformed case to keep refusing at `TELEMETRY_INPUT`.

4) FIVE LAYERS CAN ANSWER. Pin code AND layer on every refusal, and build each fixture valid at the earlier layers or a different one answers and the assertion quietly stops testing its subject.

5) UNKNOWN RENDERED AS ZERO. Blind handoffs carry UNKNOWN token and step facts. An unmeasured count and a zero count are different facts; drill 4 proves the tests notice.

6) MESSAGE ECHO. Adding interpolation to a failure message would leak provider output, a path, argv or a digest out of a failure path — the producer avoided this deliberately and the daemon must not undo it.

7) BRIDGE BYTES ARE BYTE-COMPARED. One line, LF ending. CRLF or a trailing blank line moves the file from the guard's `missing` set into `wrongContent` — still red, more confusingly.

8) DAEMON GATES RED AT BASELINE from foreign slices. Record the before-set; only the delta over the three owned files must be empty. Read the count line — exit 0 with no count line ran nothing.

9) SHARED WORKTREE. HEAD moved repeatedly this session. Re-check `git status --porcelain` before committing, commit by explicit three-path pathspec, verify with `git show --stat`, confirm the probe is deleted and every drill reverted.

10) DOWNSTREAM: task-d3239529aab54f98b31bfd3662e316bf consumes this handoff into the durable ledger and is BACKLOG pending this task. Name it in the completion so the consumer-edge rail is satisfied by a recorded id rather than an assumption.
